title: Maintenance Epoch Coordinator + Throughput Contracts for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Lena Park
description: Customers on Dedicated capacity require predictable throughput SLAs while the fleet undergoes routine maintenance (kernel upgrades, host reboots, driver updates) and occasional degraded capacity events. Current node draining and upgrade flows are ad-hoc: drains are initiated manually or by simple ramp rules, which can briefly violate throughput contracts or trigger aggressive autoscaling that increases cost. This ticket scopes a coordinated control-plane component (Maintenance Epoch Coordinator) that enforces throughput contracts, stages node lifecycle operations into bounded epochs, and coordinates with autoscaler policies to minimize both SLA impact and cost.
proposal: Introduce a Maintenance Epoch Coordinator (MEC) that manages maintenance epochs for each dedicated fleet. Each epoch is a bounded time window with a declared throughput contract (requests-per-second and p95 latency budget) and an expected capacity delta. The MEC will: 1) negotiate a throughput contract with the customer-configured policy, 2) compute a safe drain/reintegration plan across nodes in epochs, 3) signal autoscaler with a planned capacity curve to avoid reactive overprovisioning, and 4) provide observability hooks and rollback triggers. The MEC exposes APIs to schedule windows, annotate node work (software upgrade / hardware maintenance), and mark epochs as emergency or standard. It also integrates with routing fallbacks to spill traffic to compatible model variants or other regions when needed.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype MEC orchestration service + epoch concept (control plane only) and simple epoch scheduler
Phase 2: Autoscaler integration: planned capacity API and graceful scale handles
Phase 3: Node agent changes for epoch-aware drain/rejoin and staged KV cache checkpointing
Phase 4: Rollouts: canary on a non-customer fleet, then opt-in pilot customers, followed by full release
acceptance_criteria: MEC can schedule an epoch that specifies start, end, and throughput contract, and persist it to fleet config
Scheduled epochs execute node drains across a fleet without exceeding the declared throughput contract in 95% of test scenarios
Autoscaler accepts planned capacity curves from MEC and does not exceed 1.2x baseline capacity during scheduled maintenance in load tests
Node agents honor MEC drain prioritization and report drain progress and estimated time-to-ready
Console UI shows epoch timeline, impacted nodes, expected vs observed throughput, and provides abort/extend controls
tasks: Scheduler: epoch allocation algorithm to minimize simultaneous capacity loss (bin-packing by AZ + model shard affinity)
Autoscaler: plannedCapacity v1 endpoint and consumer adapter
Node agent: graceful drain handshake with checkpoint + KV cache snapshot signal
Observability: epoch metrics dashboard + alert when observed throughput deviates >15% from contract
E2E tests: simulate rolling kernel upgrades with synthetic load and measure contract adherence
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Autoscaler ignores planned curves and scales reactively -> Mitigation: add admission of planned curves with priority flag and throttle reactive scale-ups during epoch
Risk: Long drains raise p95 latency -> Mitigation: staged drain with per-node rate limits and prefix cache warmup on reintegration
Risk: Customer-configured tight throughput guarantees cannot be met -> Mitigation: MEC validates contracts against historical telemetry and rejects unrealistic windows or suggests extended windows
notes: This approach differs from one-off drain scripts by making maintenance an explicit first-class scheduling primitive tied to throughput SLAs.
We should coordinate with SRE and Dedicated sales to prepare standard contract templates and change communications for pilots.
Consider future extension: epoch-based billing adjustments (discounts or credits) if maintenance causes measurable customer-impact; put on roadmap rather than MVP.
